R001.check_point: Correct Optus drawing template has been used?
R001.explanation: Two CAD templates are available for Optus. We primarily use the standard Optus FC Template, but some projects use the Child CAD Template. If the client provides the input file in the Child CAD Template, we will use that file; otherwise, we will follow the standard Optus template.
R001.image_ref:
Optus FC template saved. 
Austin Ferry site use a Child CAD file, which is also saved
R001.dlux_notes:
Check whether the correct template (Child CAD template) is used instead of the standard one.
Child CAD template → has watermark

Standard template → no watermark

How to validate:
Check input CAD file
If input has watermark → output must use same template
R001.optus_review:
Correct

If input has no watermark → output must match with Optus standard drawing template.

R002.check_point: Drawings must be correct scale in all the sheets
R002.explanation: Check all drawing scale must be followed standard scale. If scale is not followed the standard or Acceptable, need to highlight

Ensure scale is mentioned in required sheets

First sheets (cover, antenna, etc.) → may NOT have scale

Other sheets → MUST have scale
R002.optus_review:
Ensure scale is mentioned in required sheets

Cover sheet, G1, A series, P series & E series sheet → may NOT have scale. Also no need to check the reference OSD standard sheet scale.

Other sheets → MUST have scale, must be followed the standard scale value

R003.explanation: Check shown scale must in standard one. Also scale must be matched with viewport

need CAD access, click on scale to view viewport, need to check on viewport
The mentioned scale must match actual viewport scale in CAD

R004.check_point: FC stamp is correctly mentioned to all sheets?
R004.explanation: Draft symbol must be in all sheets
R004.dlux_notes:
Check if Draft/FC stamp is present in all sheets.
Check if the DRAFT watermark is present in the drawing pages.
If DRAFT watermark is visible → PASS
If DRAFT watermark is not visible → FAIL
Do not check FOR CONSTRUCTION stamp.
R004.optus_review: Draft symbol must be RED color & same alignment (rotation) as per reference image.

R005.explanation: Main objective is existing must be in unbold layer whereas proposed must be in bold layer.
R005.image_ref: You can find the layer formats in CAD template in Model space. Refer "3-Optus FC template Layer format & 4-Child CAD template Layer format" snip
R005.dlux_notes:
Existing must be unbold, propsed means bold, Check in As-built file.
Check layer usage based on Existing vs Proposed

Existing elements → Unbold/light layer

Proposed/New elements → Bold layer
R005.optus_review:
All Headings, Notes and Structural notes must be shown in bold layers. Most of the sheets Callout/Text are bold layer, except for below exemption:

G1 sheet: 
Equipment Shelter/ODU: The heading must be bold, but the content should be unbolded unless a new cabinet is proposed or any modification is made.
Transmission: The heading must be bold, but the content should be unbolded unless a new dish or new fibre is proposed

If Callout mentions "Existing" that must be Unbold layer.

If callout mentions "Proposed/New/Relocated/Removed" that must be Bold layer

R006.explanation: All text should be in full uppercase, except for email IDs (mostly found in the G1 sheet – Construction Site Access) and units such as m (meter) and km (kilometer) & programe name (eJV) 'e' lower case accepted
R006.dlux_notes:
units of measurements will be in small, mail ID 
other than these all will be in upper case
Email ID comes under Construction Site access(most of the time)

Exceptions:
Title block (template content)
Program name like “eJV” (lowercase allowed)

Antenna schedule names should start with A1, A2, A3, etc., while plumbing diagram names should start with P1, P2, etc.

If step pegs or a ladder are available on site, access can be made using the ladder. In such cases, we must check whether the ladder has been certified within the last 1 year; otherwise, it cannot be used.

However, most projects will require an EWP. In some rare cases, the EWP cannot be used due to site constraints such as very tall buildings, narrow access roads for parking the EWP, or busy roads. This can be checked at a later stage

R037.check_point: Update the Transmission as per the As-Built (AB). These are mostly in the unbold layer unless an update is required.
R037.explanation: Check the transmission type, either fibre or dish. The site is connected to the other network via radio or fibre. Verify this through the As-Built drawings and site photos. If any active Optus dish is found, note that the site is connected via radio; otherwise, it is connected via fibre.

Validate transmission type (Dish(Radio) / Fiber)
Check presence of dish antenna in site photos
Cross-check transmission details in As-built drawings
R037.optus_review:
Correct. The preferred option is based on the as-built.

Photo validation is also acceptable, but sometimes there are additional dishes on site that belong to other carriers and not to Optus. For this site, the elevation drawing clearly mentions the Optus dish, which makes it clear. However, in some other projects, they simply mention “dish” without specifying the carrier, which makes validation difficult.
